keyVerseText: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word. Elijah: Heb. Elijahu: Gr. Elias
rootMeaning: The name אֵלִיָּה (ʼÊlîyâh) derives from the Hebrew root אֵל (ʼêl), meaning God or mighty one, combined with the theophoric element יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of the divine name Jehovah. Thus, the literal meaning of the name is "My God is Jehovah" or "Yahweh is God." This root meaning emphasizes both the strength and sovereignty of God as the foundation of the name, highlighting a personal and declarative confession of faith in the one true God beyond any idol or false deity.
usageInScripture: The word אֵלִיָּה appears 71 times in Scripture, predominantly as a proper name for the prophet Elijah, with 21 occurrences translated as "And Elijah" and 13 simply as "Elijah." It is also used to identify other individuals named Elijah, including a Benjamite and priests during the exile. The consistency in translation underscores the name's function primarily as a personal identifier, but its repeated presence in narrative contexts reflects the significant role of Elijah the prophet as God's messenger during Israel's history.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֵלִיָּה as "My God is Jehovah" anchors the identity of the prophet Elijah within a theological framework that affirms God's exclusive sovereignty and power. Elijah's life and ministry bear witness to the living God who controls nature and history, opposing idolatry and false gods. This name reminds believers that faith is not abstract but rooted in the personal God who reveals Himself and acts decisively in covenant relationship. For the Christian faith, Elijah prefigures the ultimate prophet and mediator, Jesus Christ, who embodies God's presence and authority.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 17:1, the phrase "And Elijah the Tishbite" introduces the prophet as one who stands before the LORD God of Israel, invoking God's name with authority. The name Elijah, meaning "My God is Jehovah," reinforces the prophet's role as God's representative who proclaims divine judgment and provision. The verse highlights Elijah's unique commission and dependence on the true God, setting the stage for his prophetic actions that demonstrate God's power over nature and kings.
